newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel - low sulphur stronger, high sulphur ease.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel - low sulphur stronger, high sulphur ease.

text.p: Low sulphur cracked fuel firmed on paper and a late trade while high sulphur material was narrowly weaker on poor demand.
Traders said 45,000-50,000 tonnes of low sulphur cracked material out of Scandinavia was sold at $126.50 fob NWE, taking support from firmer swaps and good interest.

"It's a touch better than swaps, but there's good demand, possibly from the U.S," said one trader. But some dealers still thought the sector balanced to long with a further two cargoes of 40,000-50,000 tonnes apiece with potential to weigh on the market.
Some traders thought the market a touch overcooked but added that the sector wanted to draw away from high sulphur and that the contango into winter had widened on paper.

High sulphur cracked cargoes were weaker by $1-2 talked around $113-115 cif NWE. "I just don't see the demand there. Premier is not buying, ESB has bought straight-run, Portugal has been tendering, so there's sufficient product," said one trader.

Straight-run continues to be available with an M-100 finding a home at two means +$4 cif NWE and an E-4 getting picked up at around formula +$3.50 cif. High sulhphur barges were $2 down on the day. -- Matthew Jones, London Newsroom +4 171 542 8980
